Date: 2027-05-27 09:12 -0700
Subject: Staged CI gating & module contract for Acme private deployment

Team / Acme procurement + EdgeScale,

Acme has asked for an accelerated private deployment (VPC + on-prem edge) and wants clarity on how our IaC artifacts will be contracted, hardened, and gated through CI before they sign the private deployment SOW. I put together an initial list of artifacts and a proposed staged gating flow — attached as module-contracts.pdf and ci-gateflow.png.

High level asks: 
- Procurement (Acme): confirm required compliance evidence and whether DocuSign acceptance is OK for the module contract.
- EdgeScale Ops: confirm the network preflight checks you need run in their staging environment.
- Internal owners: review the gating steps, call out any missing test coverage or security checks.

Proposed timeline: module contract draft -> technical sign-off (internal) -> procurement review -> DocuSign by 2027-06-10. If we need an earlier pilot window we can compress the internal sign-off to 48 hours but only if we run the full network preflight.

Attachments: module-contracts.pdf (contract language + module list), ci-gateflow.png (staged pipeline diagram), sample-ansible-role.tar.gz (example role layout).

Markus Klein
Director, Private Deployments
Redwood Inference

Thanks for the summary and attachments — that helps. A couple of questions from procurement:

Our procurement timeline is tight: we aim to return a signed DocuSign by 2027-06-14, but we'll need the appendix and the CI scope by next week to hit that. If necessary we can do a conditional signature with the appendix delivered before prod cutover.

Subject: Re: Staged CI gating & module contract for Acme private deployment

Thanks, Markus. Quick technical read and recommended edits to the gating flow. I've attached an inline checklist and referenced the sample role. Key points below: 

- Module inventory (Terraform): network (vpc, subnets, route tables), bastion, ingress-gateway, egress-proxy, node-security (policies).
- Helm artifacts: api-gateway chart, runtime-worker chart, metrics-collector chart (charts must be pinned by digest for all releases).
- Ansible roles: juju-style roles for config bootstrap (sample-ansible-role.tar.gz shows layout).

Suggested CI gates (staged):
1) Static checks: tfsec, kubeval, helm lint, ansible-lint (PR-level).
2) Unit + plan validation: terraform plan dry-run against a mocked state, helm template + kubeconform.
3) Network preflight (run in Acme staging via runner): namespace & CIDR validation, cross-VPC route test, egress path validation (this step requires EdgeScale runner access).
4) Integration smoke: deploy to isolated staging cluster (short-lived), run health probes and KV cache persistence test.
5) Security scan & artifact signing: cosign for images, artifact timestamping, and audit log export to S3 (retention per contract appendix).

What we need from EdgeScale: a small runner image with access to the Acme staging VPC to perform step 3. From procurement: explicit retention window for audit logs and whether we need HSM-backed key attestations.

I've also called out a required preflight: SR-IOV nic check for the edge hosts (if they're using passthrough NICs). If SR-IOV is present, we need an extra gating job in step 3 to validate VF quotas and VF persistence across reboots.

Laura Bennett
Senior Manager, Platform Delivery
Redwood Inference
laura_bennett@redwood.com

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>

Date: 2027-05-27 14:08 -0700
Subject: Re: Staged CI gating & module contract for Acme private deployment

Laura — good notes. Two technical clarifications and a blocker we should call out to Acme: 

1) Namespace abstraction: our current helm values assume a single-tenant namespace layout; for Acme we should add a per-tenant namespace overlay in the terraform module so helm charts don't assume cluster-global CRDs. That will be a ~1 day change but important for rollout safety.

2) Network policy enforcement: we need to ensure CNI policy (Calico/Antrea) constraints are tested in the integration smoke. Suggest we add an e2e test that asserts pod-to-pod policy and egress denies by default.

3) Blocker: if Acme requires SR-IOV passthrough on edge (as Laura mentioned), we must certify the ansible role to include driver pinning and VF persistence tasks. Without that, we can't guarantee stable VF assignments across node reprovision; this is something to call out in the contract appendix as a risk/assumption.

I'll volunteer to own the namespace overlay changes and add the e2e network policy test to our integration suite. ETA: 2 business days for the overlay + update to CI pipeline to run the extra smoke test.

—Karthik
Principal Systems Engineer
karthik_iyer@redwood.com

Appreciate the quick turn, all. Summary & next steps: 

- Laura: finalize the appendix for audit log retention, KMS integration notes, and include the SR-IOV testing requirement wording for the contract appendix.
- Karthik: please open a short-lived branch for the namespace overlays and add the e2e network-policy test (assign to INFRA-2041).
- Vanessa: coordinate with EdgeScale Ops to stand up the runner for the network preflight and share access instructions with Acme staging.
- Procurement (Acme): we'll add the appendix to the module-contracts.pdf and send the DocuSign link by 2027-06-01. If anything in the appendix is unacceptable, flag it immediately — we can follow the conditional signature path noted earlier.

I'll prepare the DocuSign packet once Laura uploads the appendix. If everyone is aligned, let's aim to have the internal technical sign-off by 2027-05-31 so procurement has time to review.

Markus Klein
Director, Private Deployments
Redwood Inference
